page.layout: One printed page, verse text in one column with a heading above; a marginal note at the upper right beside the first lines of verse.

p.i: Crescat quó tibi laus, decus perenne.
Vincenti, tibi cuncta congruunt. Nobilis typo-grafus Lug-dunensis, &c. Nam
O felix Olor! o beate celsa
Ista munera quem beant! Sed audi,
Horum tandem erit in polo ampla merces.

page.notes: Marginal note at upper right ("Nobilis typografus Lugdunensis, &c.") transcribed beside the verse. Several lines are damaged by show-through and fading: "Deiá" (possibly Deiq. with a mark), "dum sovesfateris" (probably "dum sofa vises, fateris" or similar; uncertain), "Libriid testificantur" (likely "Libri id testificantur"), and "Vitæ millia quòd" are doubtful. Ink bleed from the reverse side appears throughout the page and was not transcribed. The woodcut or decorative initial P was read as a large initial.
